Energy Department Announces $2.8 Billion Loan to Strengthen Grid Reliability and Help Lower Costs in Wyoming

The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $2.8 billion for Grid United’s Wyoming Intertie project to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability in Wyoming

Energy.gov

November 17, 2026

Estimated Read Time 

 min

WASHINGTON—
The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $2.8 billion for Grid United's Wyoming Intertie project to lower electricity costs and strengthen grid reliability in Wyoming. The project will add approximately 1.8 gigawatts (GW) of electricity transfer capacity and is estimated to deliver up to $39 billion in electricity cost savings for American families and businesses across 17 states within the Western Electricity Coordinating Council (WECC) and Southwest Power Pool (SPP) regions.
The loan advances President Trump’s Executive Order 
Strengthening the Reliability and Security of the U.S. Electric Grid
 and builds on DOE's recent 
Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades
 (SPARK) announcement.
“The Energy Department is delivering on President Trump’s promise to strengthen America’s electric grid and unleash American energy dominance,” said 
U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright
. “Projects like Wyoming Intertie will help move more American energy where it’s needed most to support our nation’s growing energy needs and power American prosperity for decades to come.”
Wyoming Intertie will double existing transfer capacity between the SPP and WECC regions, allowing more electricity to flow across Wyoming to meet growing demand and improve grid resilience during periods of high demand and extreme weather. The project will also create hundreds of construction-related jobs and long-term operations jobs, supporting local economic growth over the 30-year life of the project.
“Thanks to President Trump and Secretary Wright, EDF is financing projects that deliver real benefits to American families and businesses,” said 
EDF Director Gregory A. Beard
. “Wyoming Intertie is a prime example of how EDF’s financing can help lower electricity costs, create American jobs, and support long-term economic growth in Wyoming and across the nation.”
While this conditional commitment indicates DOE's intent to provide a loan, Grid United's Wyoming Intertie project must satisfy certain technical, legal, environmental, and financial conditions before the Department enters definitive financing documents and funds the loan.
